quarterly_data.signal: GlobalWafers reported Q2 2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) consolidated revenue of NT$152.1 hundred million, up 8.8% QoQ and down 5.0% YoY; gross profit NT$3.14 billion (gross margin 20.6%); operating income NT$1.42 billion (operating margin 9.4%); net income NT$3.78 billion (net margin 24.8%); EPS NT$7.9. First-half 2026 consolidated revenue was NT$292 hundred million, down 7.6% YoY, with gross margin 20.7%, operating margin 9.9%, net income NT$5.67 billion (net margin 19.4%) and EPS NT$11.87. The company attributes the QoQ improvement to recovering semiconductor demand and continued growth in high-end applications.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue NT$152.1 hundred million (+8.8% QoQ, -5.0% YoY); GM 20.6%; EPS NT$7.9; 1H revenue NT$292 hundred million (-7.6% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: GlobalWafers says a fire broke out on July 20 (local time) in the 8-inch line at its Novara (Italy) plant: no injuries and no environmental pollution; the damage was limited to part of the 8-inch line, the site as a whole was not damaged, most front-end process areas and equipment were not affected by flame or heat, and core IT systems kept running. Damage assessment, recovery and insurance claims are under way. Products already cross-site qualified will be supplied from other GlobalWafers sites; for products not yet qualified it is working with customers to accelerate qualification and capacity transfer. The newly built 12-inch site was not affected: construction is complete, customer qualification is progressing smoothly, and volume will ramp in line with customer qualification and market demand.
quarterly_data.figure: fire on July 20 at the Novara 8-inch line; new 12-inch site unaffected

quarterly_data.signal: GlobalWafers says demand for the new 12-inch SOI capacity at its Missouri (U.S.) site is strong, with RF-SOI and silicon photonics products gradually entering mass production.

GlobalWafers says the newly added capacity at its Utsunomiya (Japan) plant is fully in place and running at high utilization, and the plant set shipment records in June, Q2 and the first half; besides the new expansion lines, existing 12-inch utilization is full, 8-inch utilization remains high, and the recovery is gradually extending to 6-inch products. It continues to develop higher-value products including SOI, GaN, 12-inch SiC and square wafers.

connects_to.relationship: raw silicon wafers for Micron memory fabs

contracts.signal: GlobalWafers says important customer Micron is reinforcing GlobalWafers' U.S. local advanced-wafer supply through a long-term cooperation agreement and strategic funding support, which it says helps raise demand visibility and capacity-planning efficiency for its new Texas fab (the Texas fab has passed qualification at several Tier-1 customers).
